# Preface {.unnumbered}

This book is an introduction to embedded systems programming using an
STMicroelectronics STM32 microcontroller.

::: {.callout-note}
## Draft status

This book is a work in progress. Chapter content, the specific STM32 part
number/development board, and toolchain (e.g. STM32CubeIDE) used throughout
the book still need to be filled in.
:::

It is intended for readers who are new to embedded systems, and covers the
fundamentals of microcontrollers, C programming for resource-constrained
targets, general purpose input/output (GPIO), embedded programming
patterns, timers, analog-to-digital conversion, and serial communication.

## How this book is organized

The book is split into parts, each grouping related chapters:

- **Foundations** &mdash; what an embedded system is, and the C programming
  concepts needed to work with one.
- **Digital I/O and Program Structure** &mdash; controlling GPIO pins and
  structuring larger embedded programs (hardware abstraction layers, state
  machines, interrupts).
- **Peripherals** &mdash; timers, analog-to-digital conversion (ADC), and
  serial communication.

## Relationship to the MSP430 edition

This book follows the same chapter structure as the companion
[Embedded Systems with the MSP430G2553](https://github.com/) textbook, but
is written independently for the STM32 platform rather than translated
from it, since most chapter content (peripheral registers, memory maps,
toolchain) is platform-specific. See that project's README for background
on why these are maintained as separate repositories rather than one.
